pottery.notes: BRIEF PREMISE PARTLY WRONG ON GEOGRAPHY. YAY!Clay is real, open and busy, and it does run Clay Date sessions on a public scheduler exactly as the brief says. But it is not in Fishtown, and the venue's own site cannot keep its story straight: the Clay Dates page says 'in Port Richmond just north of Fishtown', while the Contact page says 'in Kensington just north of Fishtown'. Both agree it is north of Fishtown, not in it. The address 3237 Amber Street, Philadelphia PA 19134 is confirmed three ways: the site footer on every page, the Contact page, and independently inside the KilnFire API's location record (address_1 '3237 Amber Street', city Philadelphia, state PA, zip 19134). Call it River Wards / Port Richmond edge of Kensington, roughly 3 miles northeast of Center City. Four named rooms: Green Room (original, 14 wheels), Retro Room (12 wheels, 60s-70s theme, claw machine), Philly Room (newest and largest, 18 wheels, SEPTA train seat, 6 arcade games), and the Mud Club (1500 sq ft members-only). Mud Club membership includes 24/7 access, a locker, 14+ studio glazes free, KilnFire kiln notifications, discounts on monthly workshops and classes, member socials, in-studio kitchen, lounge, retail and wifi. Equipment: 16 wheels and bats, damp boxes, grinding discs and dremels, Giffin Grips, extruder, slab roller, resin/filament/clay 3-D printers, slip casting tank and molds. Bisque to cone 04, glaze to cone 6; staff and vetted work-exchange members do all loading and firing. Members buy their own clay in-house (about 6 clay bodies plus reclaim) and pay for glaze firings only. Membership is by application to community@yayclay.com and they screen for 'a solid understanding of the ceramic process and safety practices', so it is not walk-up. No walk-ins for classes either. BYOB, free arcade, climate controlled, free street parking plus a gated lot, 15 ft projector and audio for events, work is food/oven/dishwasher/microwave safe, 60-day pickup limit. They also sell supplies and repair and install kilns, which makes this the closest thing in the batch to a supply and service business as well as a studio.

pottery.notes: BRIEF PREMISE CONFIRMED, venue exists and is operating. The correct domain is thepotterygym.com (potterygym.com does not resolve). Address 1319 N Randolph St, Philadelphia, PA 19122, published in the footer of every page. The studio describes its own location precisely and usefully: 'Accessible location on the ground floor, west of Fishtown and the Market-Frankford Line in the Ludlow neighborhood.' Ludlow, not Fishtown, and ground-floor accessible. No telephone number appears anywhere on the site; contact is thepotterygym@gmail.com only, which is a real friction point for a discovery product. Self-description: 'an inclusive ceramics studio with a DIY ethos... a community of engaged clay nerds and makers that share common values in music, style, and social causes.' Smallest and scrappiest of the four: 1000 sq ft shared member space plus a separate studio space for private events. Positions itself on price, not prestige: $140 three-week wheel workshop, $10/hr sliding-scale open studio paid in cash or Venmo, $55/month remote membership. Membership at $150/month matches YAY!Clay's Mud Club exactly, but The Pottery Gym includes unlimited shop clay and glazes and all firings in that figure while YAY!Clay charges for clay and glaze firings on top, so The Pottery Gym is materially the cheaper membership. Site footer copyright still reads 2025 and the Smoke-N-Sculpt page advertises spring dates with no year, so parts of the site are not maintained. The newsletter block is visibly misconfigured ('This newsletter signup form needs a storage option'), another sign of light upkeep. External links on the site point to clay4pay.com/gay4clay and to designer heatherjackson.io.

pottery.booking: ProClass online registration at https://reg137.imperisoft.com/Fleisher/Search/Registration.aspx. Every program has a stable, server-rendered, crawlable detail URL of the form https://reg137.imperisoft.com/Fleisher/ProgramDetail/<id>/Registration.aspx, and a full catalog index at https://reg137.imperisoft.com/Fleisher/Sitemap/Registration.aspx. Registration for fall tuition-bearing classes opened Monday July 6 at 8:00 AM; spring workshops list their own opening date (for example Ceramic Charms opens Tuesday, October 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM).
pottery.notes: BRIEF PREMISE CONFIRMED on all counts. 719 Catharine Street is correct (full form 719 Catharine Street, Philadelphia, PA 19147-2811) and kind = school is correct: ceramics is one of roughly a dozen media. Of 442 programs in Fleisher's catalog, 41 are ceramics or clay. This is by far the richest published ceramics price data in the batch, and Fleisher is the only venue of the four that publishes a complete price list, a member price, a studio fee and a firing fee for every single class. Structure of their pricing: a 10-week adult wheel class is $325 tuition non-member / $295 member for Fall 2026, plus a $50 studio fee, so $375 all in. Winter 2027 classes drop to $295 / $275 plus $50. Five-session classes are $205 / $185 plus $50. One-day workshops carry no tuition at all, just a $35 studio fee plus a $10 firing fee, which makes a three-hour Saturday intro wheel session $45 all in and the cheapest sampler in the batch by a wide margin. Ceramics Open Studio for a full term is $165 / $150 member plus a $50 studio fee. The studio fee covers glazes and firing; students buy their own clay and no outside clay is permitted (it can be bought online or at Fleisher's front desk). Fleisher also runs genuinely tuition-free ceramics classes (Handbuilding, Sculptural Forms, Traditional Nigerian Pottery) where the only charge is the $50 studio fee, and access to tuition-free adult classes is the headline benefit of the $65 adult membership, so $65 + $50 buys a full 10-week Wednesday handbuilding class. That is the single best value found anywhere in this batch. Raku (3 Day + Firing) is the exception with a $100 firing fee on top of $150 tuition and a $50 studio fee. Tuition assistance is offered every term. Firing turnaround is about one week. Unclaimed bisque or glaze work is held one term only and greenware is discarded. Ceramics studio is elevator accessible with some stairs in auxiliary areas; accommodations via adulteducation@fleisher.org. Fall 2026 term runs September 8 to November 20; Winter 2027 term runs early January to early March. Fleisher also has a BigCartel shop (fleisherartmemorial.bigcartel.com) and an eTapestry donation platform, and the Inquirer reported in July 2026 on Etsy Center for Crafts grants involving them.

KilnFire is a Laravel app with a fully machine-readable JSON API: POST /classes/data returns organization, class templates, instructor names and bios; POST /classes/calendar-data returns dated sessions with start/end times, prices in cents, meeting counts and seat limits. Both need a session cookie plus the X-XSRF-TOKEN from the cookie jar (GET /classes/ first); no login or key. This is the single best machine-readable pottery schedule found in this zone. INFERENCE: kilnfire.com also runs a public studio directory, so it is likely usable as a multi-venue source. Phone number not published on the Squarespace site; contact is info@rebelpotters.org. The Finder at https://www.phila.gov/parks-rec-finder/ is a 1KB JS shell, but its bundle (build.js) names the backend: https://phl.carto.com/api/v2/sql over tables ppr_programs, ppr_facilities, ppr_program_schedules, ppr_days, ppr_activity_categories. I queried it directly this run. ppr_programs carries program_name, fee, fee_frequency, age_range, registration_status, program_is_active, program_is_public and a facility id array; ppr_program_schedules carries date_from, date_to, day ids, time_from and time_to; ppr_days maps the day ids (56fc90d38041752020119b23 = Monday, weekday_number 2; 56fc90e5b67a9db679a60d03 = Tuesday, weekday_number 3, both read from the table itself). TRAP: times are stored as 2012-01-01T19:00:00Z style timestamps, i.e. a dummy date with the real local wall-clock time; do not treat them as UTC. TRAP 2: schedule rows are never deleted, so you must take the max date_to per program, and many 'Registering' programs have no schedule newer than 2023. City-wide there are 36 ceramics/pottery/clay programs in the table and 16 that are both active and public; Starr Garden is the only Center City site among them and it holds two of the sixteen. EVIDENCE for the site: ppr_facilities public_name 'Starr Garden', address '600-44 Lombard St Philadelphia, PA 19147', contact_phone 2156861782, site_status 'Open regular schedule'. UNCONFIRMED: whether there is a wheel or only handbuilding, whether a kiln is on site, and whether either class is running this term. CHEAPEST NEXT CHECK: call 215-686-1782.

Platform detail: WordPress site (wp-content, wp-json present); /wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events returns 404 so The Events Calendar is not installed. ActiveNet API probing: GET https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/wayneart/rest/activity/detail/14490?locale=en-US returns clean JSON with activity name, season ('Adult Fall 2026'), category ('4. Adult Ceramics'), activity number, first/last date, session count and structured instructor records, but NO fee fields. POST to /rest/activity/list (the search endpoint that does carry fees) returned HTTP 302 both with and without a cookie jar and the page's __csrfToken, so the priced list could not be read. That is the cheapest remaining way to get Wayne's prices programmatically.

Plus the two things almost nobody else publishes: an open-studio day rate ($10) and per-bag clay prices ($45 porcelain / $30 other). Platform is Drupal 7 era (sites/all/themes/scholarly), not WordPress, so no wp-json and no tribe endpoint exists. Registration hands off to Active Network. 13 clay offerings listed for Fall 2026, adult and youth. Fall session runs Sept 14 - Nov 9, 2026, so a second winter session is likely. Caveat: the 13 classes above were the Fall session; class node URLs carry a trailing sequence number (e.g. -22, -14) that changes between sessions, so a scraper should crawl /classes/ceramic-arts rather than remember URLs.

Without the cookie jar the POST returns 302. There is no JSON feed. The portal exposes three semesters in its filter: '2026-2027 FNL Season', 'Fall 2026' and 'Kiln Firings 2026', confirming standalone kiln-firing registrations.
